title: Dispatched Study Abroad at Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
paragraphs: In this year's dispatched study abroad, I did a clerkship of about two months at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

First, I was allowed to do a two-week clerkship in the Department of Traditional Chinese Medicine at Ruijin Hospital. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is widely used in Japan as well, in the form of kampo and acupuncture and moxibustion. However, I think that in reality not many people know the basic ideas of TCM or how it is treated in its home, China. I chose this department in order to fill that gap through this study abroad. The doctors of the TCM department carefully explained its way of thinking and its diagnosis and treatment. In addition, the local students guided me to a community hospital as well, and I took part in actual acupuncture and moxibustion treatment.

Next I took part in a clerkship in nephrology at Renji Hospital East Campus. Here I received lectures mixed in with the students and had the opportunity to observe PD and HD procedures. The dialysis room was extremely huge, and the sight of what must have been 60 dialysis machines running at the same time was overwhelming and made me feel the scale of the country of China.

Finally, I continued with a clerkship in gastroenterology at Renji Hospital. The gastroenterology department of this hospital was said to be among the best and most authoritative in China. It was roughly divided into three teams, "gastrointestinal diseases," "hepatitis" and "endoscopy," and I was allowed to rotate through them one week each. I learned a lot in each team, but what impressed me greatly was the fast tempo of endoscopy examinations. The doctors performed endoscopy at an abnormal speed that would be unthinkable in Japan. Even now I can hardly believe that they handled nearly 40 patients in one room in the morning alone.

The above is my impression of the clerkship, but I think my life on weekends and after the clerkship was also very fulfilling. The students of Jiao Tong University guided me to various places and we were able to deepen our friendship. I also became very close with students who were studying abroad from other countries in the same way, partly because our circumstances were similar. Sometimes sharing religious and political discussions broadened my values. The city of Shanghai is currently in a bubble, and the economic situation could be seen even from the people walking in the streets. I was also able to feel firsthand how national policies different from Japan's affect people's lives and the townscape. Besides that, I traveled not only in Shanghai but to many cities and mountains.

Overall, I feel I was given a very fruitful study abroad. I think it is a reality that, owing to differences in national policy, the level of medical care and the number of hospitals that can provide advanced medicine are still insufficient. However, I am convinced that the TCM experience mentioned above and China's unique sense of medicine will give breadth to my life as a doctor from now on. Also, life in unfamiliar China, the reality of socialism, and interaction with other exchange students and local students stimulated me and became a good opportunity to look at myself again. In fact I encountered many dangerous things, but even those became good experiences. I am very grateful.
